enriched.summary: A aula aborda gramática, vocabulário e pronúncia em inglês, com foco em verbos irregulares, formação de frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas no Present Simple, além de expressões e palavras úteis para o dia a dia. Exercícios práticos ajudam os alunos a aplicar os conceitos aprendidos.

vocabulary.definition: A group of people working together toward a common goal.
examples: Most of the team completed the task.
Our team won the competition.
I go to the gym once a week.
She washes her car once a week.

vocabulary.definition: A short, commonly known phrase that offers advice or wisdom.
examples: There's a saying that goes 'Actions speak louder than words.'
I get very nervous and anxious before exams.
She felt anxious about the meeting.

vocabulary.definition: The act of preserving or keeping something in good condition.
examples: The machine requires regular maintenance.
Building maintenance is essential.

vocabulary.definition: A person with whom one works in a professional setting.
examples: My colleague helped me finish the project.
She is a colleague at the office.

vocabulary.definition: To use time in an unproductive or inefficient way.
examples: Don’t waste time on unnecessary tasks.
He tends to waste time watching TV all day.

vocabulary.definition: A device or situation intended to catch or trick someone.
examples: The hunters set a trap for the animals.
Don’t fall into the trap of procrastination.

vocabulary.definition: The son of one’s brother or sister.
examples: My nephew loves playing soccer.
She bought a gift for her nephew.

vocabulary.definition: The daughter of one’s brother or sister.
examples: My niece is very talented in arts.
Her niece graduated last year.

grammar.explanation: The Present Simple tense is used to describe habits, facts, and general truths.
rules: Add -s or -es to verbs in the third person singular (he/she/it).
Use 'do' or 'does' for questions and negatives.
examples: Jane speaks German at work.
Jane doesn’t speak German at work.
Does Jane speak German at work?
commonMistakes: Forgetting to add -s/-es in the third person singular.
Using incorrect auxiliary verbs in questions and negatives.

expressions.usage: Used to refer to the majority of a group.
examples: Most of the team agreed to the plan.

practiceQuestions.question: Does Jane speak German at work?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The question asks about Jane’s ability to speak German at work in the Present Simple tense.

practiceQuestions.question: What language does Jane speak at work?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The question inquires about the language Jane speaks at work, requiring a factual answer.

culturalNotes: In English-speaking countries, colleagues are often addressed by their first names, even in professional settings.
Social media influencers often shape public opinion in English-speaking cultures.
studyTips: Practice forming sentences in the Present Simple to solidify your understanding.
Use flashcards to memorize vocabulary with translations and example sentences.

Once a week (Uma vez por semana)
I get very nervous / anxious. (Eu fico muito nervoso / ansioso.)
